title: Thompson's Station TN Housing Market Update: November 2026
description: See what Redfin, Zillow and Realtor.com data shows for the Thompson's Station TN housing market: days on market, months of supply and price.
body:
If you are watching the Thompson's Station TN housing market, the three big data sources do not all say the same thing in the same words. Redfin reports sales and inventory. Zillow publishes a market temperature index. Realtor.com scores how hot a county is. Here is what each one shows right now and how to read them together.

I am Scott Davis, a REALTOR® with Hive Nashville. This is a plain look at the numbers, not a forecast.

## The Thompson's Station numbers from Redfin

{{img:0}}

According to the [Redfin Data Center](https://www.redfin.com/news/data-center/), as of September 30, 2026, using a rolling three-month window, Thompson's Station looks like this:

- Median sale price: $833,246, up 1.7% from a year earlier
- Median days on market: 65
- Average sale-to-list ratio: 99.0%
- Active listings: 151
- Months of supply: 5.8

A median is the middle sale, so it moves with the mix of homes that happened to sell. A small town can see that mix shift from one period to the next. Treat the price as a snapshot, not a verdict on any one home.

For a running view of local figures, see our [Thompson's Station housing market data](/thompsons-station/housing-market) page.

## What Zillow and Realtor.com add

Our data files give Thompson's Station an overall rating of Buyer's market. Zillow Research puts its Market Temperature Index for the area at 25. Zillow's index also fell by 21 over three months, which is why the trend reads as cooling. You can find the underlying series at Zillow Research.

Realtor.com works at the county level. [Realtor.com Research](https://www.realtor.com/research/data/) shows Williamson County with a hotness score of 40.5 out of 100. That is a county figure, so it blends Thompson's Station with other Williamson County cities.

These measures are built differently, so they will not always line up exactly. That is normal. When several of them point the same direction, as the cooling trend does here, that is more informative than any single number.

## How to read the three terms that matter most

{{img:1}}

Three terms come up in almost every market report. Here is what each one means.

**Months of supply.** This is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace of sales. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 months is balanced, and over 6 months favors buyers. At 5.8, Thompson's Station sits just inside the balanced band by that rule of thumb, close to the buyer side. The overall Buyer's market rating in our files and the months of supply figure are not saying exactly the same thing, and that is a good reminder to look at several measures.

**Days on market.** This is how long homes take to go under contract. A median of 65 days means half of the homes sold took less time and half took more. It is a market-wide middle, and any single home can sit far from it depending on price, condition and presentation.

**Sale-to-list ratio.** This compares the final sale price with the last list price. At 99.0%, the average sale in the Redfin window closed close to the asking price. That tells you how much room there was between list and sale on average. It does not tell you how much room there is on a particular home.

## Thompson's Station next to metro Nashville

For a wider frame, Redfin's Nashville metro figures for the four weeks ending November 1, 2026 show a median sale price of $468,307, median days on market of 68, a sale-to-list ratio of 97.6%, months of supply of 5.9, and 2,213 homes sold.

The two sets of numbers cover different windows, a rolling three months versus four weeks, so compare them loosely. The point is that conditions are not identical from one place to the next. National headlines and even metro averages can miss what is happening in a single city or price range. If you are choosing between cities, you can look at nearby pages for [Franklin](/franklin/housing-market), [Spring Hill](/spring-hill/housing-market) and the [Nashville housing market](/nashville/housing-market), or the broader [market data for the I-65 corridor](/market-data).

School assignment and property taxes depend on the exact address. For any home you are serious about, check with the school district and the county directly.

## Mortgage rates are part of the picture

The 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.18% for the week of November 5, 2026, according to Freddie Mac via FRED. Nobody can reliably predict where rates go next, so I will not try. What you can do is see what that rate means for a monthly payment on a price you have in mind. The [mortgage calculator](/mortgage-calculator) lets you test different prices and down payments.

A payment that fits comfortably in your budget, with an emergency fund left after closing, is a steadier guide than trying to time the market. Lenders can walk you through your own numbers, and you are free to choose any lender you like.

## What to take from the data

Here is the short version for Thompson's Station as of the latest figures:

- Zillow's index shows a cooling trend over the last three months.
- Redfin's months of supply is close to the buyer end of the balanced range.
- Homes took a median of 65 days to sell and closed near list price on average.
- Prices were up 1.7% from a year earlier, so the picture is mixed rather than one-directional.

None of that guarantees what happens next, and none of it describes any particular home. The useful move is to look at the specific home, its price history, and your own finances.

## Next step

If you are thinking about buying in Thompson's Station or nearby, you can [get matched with homes](/buy#form). After you fill out the form, I schedule a call and we will be talking within the next 48 hours. If you own a home and want a sense of its value, you can [find out what your home is worth](/sell#form). Either way, I will walk through the local data with you and answer questions without pressure.

faq.q: Is Thompson's Station a buyer's market right now?
faq.a: Our data files rate Thompson's Station a Buyer's market. Redfin's months of supply is 5.8 as of September 30, 2026, which sits in the 4 to 6 month balanced band by the common rule of thumb, so different measures read slightly differently.

faq.q: What is the median home price in Thompson's Station?
faq.a: Redfin reports a median sale price of $833,246 as of September 30, 2026, up 1.7% from a year earlier, based on a rolling three-month window.

faq.q: How long do homes take to sell in Thompson's Station?
faq.a: Redfin shows a median of 65 days on market as of September 30, 2026. The average sale-to-list ratio was 99.0%.

faq.q: What does months of supply mean?
faq.a: It is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace of sales. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 is balanced, and over 6 favors buyers.

faq.q: What is the current 30-year mortgage rate?
faq.a: Freddie Mac via FRED reported 7.18% for the week of November 5, 2026. Rates change weekly, and your own rate depends on your lender and finances.

issues: Article 12 / unsupported claim: "When several of them point the same direction, as the cooling trend does here, that is more informative than any single number." The supplied facts show a cooling trend only in the Zillow index. The Redfin and Realtor.com figures give no trend, so the sentence wrongly implies several measures agree. It also offers a loose interpretive rule that the facts do not support.

Article 12 / missing context for statistics: "Here is what each one shows right now". The Zillow Market Temperature Index (25, -21 over three months) and the Realtor.com hotness score (40.5 of 100) are given with no as-of date. "Right now" in a November post overstates how current them figures are, since the supplied data dates to September 30, 2026.

Article 12 / unsubstantiated rating: "Our data files give Thompson's Station an overall rating of Buyer's market." The same rating appears in the FAQ: "Our data files rate Thompson's Station a Buyer's market." The rating's source, methodology and date are not identified, so readers cannot verify it. It also conflicts with the post's own 5.8 months-of-supply reading, which falls in the balanced band.
